papers.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
papers.excerpt: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations.
papers.tldr: asmaNet is presented, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior, for gravitational-wave population studies and results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications.

papers.title: Beyond Point Photo-$z$ Estimates: Normalizing Flows for Tomographic $N(z)$ Reconstruction with DESI DR1
papers.excerpt: Accurate calibration of tomographic redshift distributions, $N(z)$ is essential for cosmological analysis of weak lensing data.

papers.title: Contrastive Astromer: Two-Stage Contrastive Representation Learning for Astronomical Light Curve Classification
papers.excerpt: Large astronomical surveys collect abundant light curves, but reliable class labels remain scarce.
papers.tldr: Results show that contrastive adaptation makes pretrained light-curve representations more effective for classification and more informative about the structure of variability classes.

papers.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
papers.excerpt: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres.
papers.tldr: This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations.

papers.title: Learned Surrogates of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
papers.excerpt: Three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, the flow of astrophysical and fusion plasmas, is costly to simulate.

papers.title: The Agentic Observer Hackathon: Autonomous Decision-making in Simulated Astronomical Surveys
papers.excerpt: Astronomical surveys must allocate observing time while responding to changing conditions and competing scientific priorities.
papers.tldr: This work evaluates systems submitted by 102 teams on campaigns reserved for evaluation and analyse target completion in a reference campaign, finding the leading systems combine numerical exposure planning with language models for interpreting operational information and supporting longer-term decisions.

papers.title: Two Fast Radio Burst Candidates Detected in the RATAN-600 Blind Survey
papers.comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Accepted to Astrophysical Bulletin, 2026, v.81, N.4
papers.excerpt: We report the detection of two single dispersed pulses with widths of about 6.7\,ms and 15.6\,ms and flux densities of about 0.8 and 1.7\,Jy.

papers.title: SHAPE: Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions A machine learning approach to solar flare forecasting
papers.excerpt: Solar flares are the most energetic impulsive events in the solar system, and reliable operational forecasting of the rarest and most destructive M- and X-class events remains an open problem.
papers.tldr: Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions (SHAPE), a two-phase deep-learning pipeline that bypasses sunspot proxies in favour of direct soft X-ray observations from the GOES X-ray Sensor, shows that competitive flare forecasting is achievable with compact architectures that retain in minutes on standard hardware, without sunspot proxy inputs.
